scenarios.title: Sign-in interrupts a meal choice
scenarios.trigger: A guest configures a dish and is asked to verify identity.
scenarios.expected: Preserve choices, context, and return target. After verification return to the dish or checkout, refresh price/stock, and require a new commitment if anything material changed.

scenarios.title: Expired or repeated verification codes
scenarios.trigger: The customer uses an expired code or requests many codes.
scenarios.expected: Show an actionable expiry/rate-limit state with safe retry and recovery. Do not expose whether another account exists or indefinitely lock an active order out of support.

scenarios.title: Private order deep link
scenarios.trigger: A link to an order is opened under the wrong account.
scenarios.expected: Require the authorized account and deny private content. Link previews, error text, analytics, and redirects must not reveal order, recipient, or household details.

scenarios.title: Guest and account carts collide
scenarios.trigger: A returning account already has a basket when guest verification completes.
scenarios.expected: Show both contexts and ask which draft to keep or restore. Never combine kitchens, silently double quantities, or treat either draft as reserved inventory.

scenarios.title: Deleted meal or expired campaign link
scenarios.trigger: A shared link references removed content or an ended offer.
scenarios.expected: Explain unavailability and offer current eligible discovery. Do not crash, resurrect an expired price, or redirect to an unrelated meal as though it were the original.

scenarios.title: Location permission denied
scenarios.trigger: The customer declines GPS or approximate location is inaccurate.
scenarios.expected: Provide manual search/pin/address entry with equal access. The phone position remains a suggestion and cannot overwrite a confirmed delivery destination.

scenarios.title: Outdated address search response
scenarios.trigger: The customer types a new destination while a previous request is still running.
scenarios.expected: Version or cancel responses; only the latest intended destination updates results. Confirm the pin and locality before replacing the shopping context.

scenarios.title: Address change invalidates basket
scenarios.trigger: A new address changes eligible kitchens, slots, or fees.
scenarios.expected: Preview affected lines and the new quote. Let the customer retain the old destination or review the changed basket; do not silently delete or charge it.

scenarios.title: Address book edited during delivery
scenarios.trigger: The customer edits a saved address after an order is confirmed.
scenarios.expected: Update future defaults only. The active order retains its accepted address snapshot and any actual delivery change follows the reviewed amendment process.

scenarios.title: Pin outside supported boundary
scenarios.trigger: A plausible text address has a pin beyond the delivery polygon or inaccessible route.
scenarios.expected: Block commitment, explain serviceability, and offer pin correction or a valid destination. No payment can create an unfulfillable order.

scenarios.title: Midnight changes relative labels
scenarios.trigger: A basket opened before midnight is resumed the next day.
scenarios.expected: Render absolute accepted dates and recalculate availability. Do not reinterpret a stored date as the new tomorrow or move an existing order.

scenarios.title: Cutoff closes while reviewing
scenarios.trigger: A customer reaches payment after the slot cutoff with an old quote.
scenarios.expected: Enforce server time, shorten/expire reservations correctly, and offer a valid slot. Do not trust the client countdown or accept a new late commitment.

scenarios.title: Slot fills during browsing
scenarios.trigger: Other confirmed orders consume the remaining delivery/production capacity.
scenarios.expected: Refresh eligibility and offer the next actual slot with basket effects. No charge occurs for the full slot.

scenarios.title: Date change changes supply
scenarios.trigger: A favorite kitchen has different dishes on the newly selected day.
scenarios.expected: Retain intent as a draft, identify unavailable lines, and ask for valid replacements. Revalidate prices, options, cutoffs, and promotion eligibility.

scenarios.title: Express collection has stale eligibility
scenarios.trigger: An item looked express-eligible before its batch or courier capacity changed.
scenarios.expected: Recheck batch life, preparation, route, and courier capacity. Remove the express promise or offer a valid scheduled alternative before commitment.

scenarios.title: New user has no order history
scenarios.trigger: The customer has no favorites, reviews, or previous orders.
scenarios.expected: Show real serviceable discovery and onboarding guidance. Omit empty personalized modules and do not fabricate popular meals, ratings, or past behavior.

scenarios.title: Promotional banner targets another context
scenarios.trigger: An offer exists but is invalid for the selected date, address, or variant.
scenarios.expected: Show eligibility accurately and route to the valid context with consent. Do not present an ineligible headline price as the payable price.

scenarios.title: Several active orders exist
scenarios.trigger: The customer has multiple upcoming or checking-payment records.
scenarios.expected: Provide clear order selection and individual status. A new basket remains independent; no alert or status card overwrites another order.

scenarios.title: Bottom overlays hide content
scenarios.trigger: A sticky cart, tab bar, keyboard, or system inset overlaps a product or action.
scenarios.expected: Reserve safe layout space and maintain accessible scrolling/focus. Portion, price, required errors, and primary actions remain reachable.

scenarios.title: Cached home after supply pause
scenarios.trigger: A kitchen is paused while an older home remains cached.
scenarios.expected: Refresh visible eligibility and revalidate every add/checkout. Cached marketing content cannot bypass a seller or safety stop-sale.

scenarios.title: Arabic and transliterated names
scenarios.trigger: A buyer searches common spelling variants or mixed Arabic/English dish names.
scenarios.expected: Retrieve reviewed relevant matches while preserving original display names. Do not turn ingredient search into an allergen-free or medical suitability guarantee.

scenarios.title: Responses arrive out of order
scenarios.trigger: An older broad query returns after a newer specific query.
scenarios.expected: Display results for the current query/context only. Add actions use stable IDs, not positions in a stale list.

scenarios.title: Empty results have different causes
scenarios.trigger: A phrase has no match, a slot has no supply, or the network failed.
scenarios.expected: Show the specific state and relevant recovery: edit query, clear filter, change date, or retry. Do not report network failure as absence of kitchens.

scenarios.title: Kitchen-scoped search mistaken for global
scenarios.trigger: The buyer searches inside one kitchen and expects all sellers.
scenarios.expected: Label the current scope and provide an explicit global-search action that preserves query and delivery context.

scenarios.title: Result becomes unavailable before adding
scenarios.trigger: A result meal is unpublished, sold out, or held after the search response.
scenarios.expected: Revalidate on action, explain the changed state, and show eligible alternatives. Never add an obsolete recipe version silently.

scenarios.title: Different portion sizes sorted as price
scenarios.trigger: Results include individual plates, small variants, and family trays.
scenarios.expected: Label comparable units and from-prices. Sorting cannot imply a smaller portion is better value than a differently measured meal without a valid comparison.

scenarios.title: Ingredient filter misread as allergy safety
scenarios.trigger: A customer filters vegetarian ingredients or excludes an ingredient term.
scenarios.expected: State the filter scope and provide reviewed allergen/cross-contact information. Unsupported allergy guarantees cannot be inferred from search metadata.

scenarios.title: Filter combination yields zero results
scenarios.trigger: Several otherwise valid filters eliminate all current supply.
scenarios.expected: Show active filters and an easy reset or targeted relaxation. Keep date/address stable and distinguish no supply from a technical failure.

scenarios.title: Counts remain stale after context change
scenarios.trigger: A category count was computed for another address or date.
scenarios.expected: Refresh counts and visible results together. Do not claim currently deliverable kitchens from an unfiltered global total.

scenarios.title: Nearest kitchen cannot deliver soonest
scenarios.trigger: A nearby kitchen is busy while another has an earlier valid slot.
scenarios.expected: Treat proximity and arrival as different sort signals. Honor preparation, route, and delivery capacity instead of equating distance with speed.

scenarios.title: Closed now but future slots exist
scenarios.trigger: A cook is not operating immediately but accepts tomorrow preorders.
scenarios.expected: Show the next valid date and reviewed menu. Avoid both a misleading open promise and a blanket closed screen that hides valid future ordering.

scenarios.title: Kitchen safety or eligibility hold
scenarios.trigger: A hold is applied after customers open the kitchen page.
scenarios.expected: Block new commitments and affected dispatches; list existing orders for review. No deep link, cached page, or quick-add path bypasses the hold.

scenarios.title: New cook has no ratings
scenarios.trigger: An assessed kitchen has no eligible customer reviews.
scenarios.expected: Show a truthful new/unrated state and assessment explanation. Do not manufacture a five-star rating or imply official certification.

scenarios.title: Profile leaks a private production address
scenarios.trigger: Public profile data includes household coordinates or identifying metadata.
scenarios.expected: Return only approved public location/disclosures. Exact private pickup details remain server-restricted to authorized operational roles.

scenarios.title: Menu navigation loses place
scenarios.trigger: The user taps a section, opens a meal, then closes it.
scenarios.expected: Keep section/scroll behavior consistent and restore position. The compact header and active chip remain accessible without covering items.

scenarios.title: Required choices unresolved
scenarios.trigger: The customer taps quick add on a meal with size/protein/sauce requirements.
scenarios.expected: Open configuration, identify required groups, enforce minimum/maximum choices, and block an invalid add. Never guess a safety-relevant ingredient choice.

scenarios.title: Variant promotion differs by size
scenarios.trigger: Only one weight has a discount and quantity changes.
scenarios.expected: Show that selected variant price and full line total. Recalculate stock and discounts; do not spread the offer to every size.

scenarios.title: Distinct configurations merged
scenarios.trigger: Two units of one dish have different sauces or proteins.
scenarios.expected: Keep separate lines and production instructions. Only identical recipe/variant/modifier/slot configurations may merge.

scenarios.title: Ingredient changes during configuration
scenarios.trigger: A cook changes a recipe after the customer opens its sheet.
scenarios.expected: Revalidate version and disclosures before commitment. Require acceptance of a material change or keep the accepted safe version where valid.

scenarios.title: Allergen request in free text
scenarios.trigger: A note asks for guaranteed absence of an allergen or unsupported ingredient substitution.
scenarios.expected: Do not treat the note as an accepted safety change. Provide approved information, route to qualified review, or decline the unsupported request.

scenarios.title: Second kitchen added
scenarios.trigger: A buyer with an active kitchen basket adds another seller item.
scenarios.expected: Offer keep current or explicit save/replace. Do not silently create a second delivery, combined order, or extra fee.

scenarios.title: Draft resumed after cutoff
scenarios.trigger: A persisted basket is opened after its stock/window/quote expired.
scenarios.expected: Explain affected lines, refresh availability/prices, and offer a valid date. The saved draft is not treated as reserved inventory.

scenarios.title: Last line removed
scenarios.trigger: The customer decrements the final unit or clears the basket.
scenarios.expected: Use confirmation or a safe undo pattern and an honest empty state. Do not leave a stale sticky total or accidental checkout capability.

scenarios.title: Add-more loses kitchen/date
scenarios.trigger: The customer returns from cart to browse more meals.
scenarios.expected: Restore the originating kitchen, section, scroll position, and selected window. Another context requires an explicit choice.

scenarios.title: Same cart edited on two devices
scenarios.trigger: Concurrent updates change quantities or options.
scenarios.expected: Detect cart version conflict, return current state, and explain refresh. A stale client cannot overwrite a newer accepted configuration or double an order.

scenarios.title: Delivery price is still unknown
scenarios.trigger: Address or window has not been selected.
scenarios.expected: Label the displayed sum as food subtotal and request missing context. Block payment commitment until an exact complete quote is reviewed.

scenarios.title: Coupon threshold lost after edit
scenarios.trigger: Removing a line takes the basket below a promotion or minimum.
scenarios.expected: Recalculate and explain the discount/fee change before commitment. Preserve accurate sponsor allocation and seller proceeds.

scenarios.title: Offer expires during checkout
scenarios.trigger: An accepted-looking coupon or quote expires before the order reserves/commits.
scenarios.expected: Apply the defined server expiry, issue a fresh quote, and request acceptance of a material difference. No silent higher charge.

scenarios.title: Partial refund of discounted item
scenarios.trigger: A sponsored item is missing from a paid order.
scenarios.expected: Refund the allocated amount actually paid and associated applicable amounts. Reverse sponsor/commission/seller entries consistently without over-refund or double recovery.

scenarios.title: Several households share one address
scenarios.trigger: Fraud checks see several legitimate accounts at a compound/building.
scenarios.expected: Apply contextual abuse review and an appeal. Do not automatically deny valid customer rights or safety remedies solely because an address is shared.

scenarios.title: Two customers buy the last portion
scenarios.trigger: Both checkout requests pass client-side availability.
scenarios.expected: Database-level commitment allows only the available quantity. The losing request gets a useful refresh/alternative and no impossible charge.

scenarios.title: Shared kitchen or delivery cap exhausted
scenarios.trigger: Dish stock exists but oven/labor or courier-window capacity is full.
scenarios.expected: Evaluate every capacity constraint atomically or with a safe durable reservation. Item stock alone cannot authorize the order.

scenarios.title: Reservation expires while bank screen is open
scenarios.trigger: The displayed reservation timer ends before payment returns.
scenarios.expected: Release once, keep payment outcome separate, and reconcile late provider results. Never presume reservation expiry means funds did not move.

scenarios.title: Missing recipient or access details
scenarios.trigger: The customer provides a pin but no deliverable building/contact details.
scenarios.expected: Validate required information clearly before commitment and preserve the draft. Do not create an order that operations cannot reach.

scenarios.title: Context changed on checkout return
scenarios.trigger: The app resumes after address, date, method, or eligibility changed.
scenarios.expected: Retrieve authoritative context/order state and revalidate quote/capacity. Do not submit a backgrounded stale checkout automatically.

scenarios.title: Provider timeout with uncertain charge
scenarios.trigger: The app cannot tell whether the provider accepted a payment.
scenarios.expected: Keep the existing attempt pending/checking, display a reference, and reconcile authoritatively. Do not invite another charge while the first outcome is unknown.

scenarios.title: Double tap and duplicate webhook
scenarios.trigger: The same customer action/provider success is delivered repeatedly.
scenarios.expected: Use idempotency and unique provider references to create at most one commitment and correct ledger impact. Return the existing outcome.

scenarios.title: Late success cannot fulfill
scenarios.trigger: Payment succeeds after expiry and stock, cutoff, or kitchen eligibility now fails.
scenarios.expected: Do not overbook or move the date. Void/refund through the approved provider flow and expose the unresolved financial state until confirmed.

scenarios.title: Invalid amount, currency, or callback
scenarios.trigger: A spoofed/replayed event or mismatched amount arrives.
scenarios.expected: Reject unauthorized transitions, preserve investigation evidence, and reconcile safely. The client return page is never trusted as payment proof.

scenarios.title: App dies after payment
scenarios.trigger: The customer closes or loses the app before confirmation renders.
scenarios.expected: Recover the same server-side order/attempt after sign-in. Correctly distinguish confirmed, checking, failed, or void/refund pending without asking for blind repayment.

scenarios.title: Events arrive out of order
scenarios.trigger: A delayed preparing event arrives after courier collection or delivery.
scenarios.expected: Apply valid transition/version rules, preserve chronology, and do not regress the visible authoritative state. Financial status remains separately modeled.

scenarios.title: Marked delivered but not received
scenarios.trigger: A courier marks handoff complete while the customer disputes receipt.
scenarios.expected: Open an urgent case, inspect custody/proof, and provide a real next action. Do not treat map proximity as proof or automatically close the dispute.

scenarios.title: Scheduled delivery arrives too early
scenarios.trigger: A courier reaches the customer substantially before the agreed window.
scenarios.expected: Treat it as a service exception and seek a safe agreed resolution. The customer is not presumed available outside the accepted window.

scenarios.title: Live location unavailable
scenarios.trigger: The partner GPS stream stops or is not integrated.
scenarios.expected: Show recorded stage and last update honestly, provide support, and avoid a fabricated moving courier or unsupported ETA precision.

scenarios.title: Failed payment hidden from history
scenarios.trigger: No meal was accepted but a hold/refund remains unresolved.
scenarios.expected: Keep the financial attempt discoverable with its outcome and case access. Do not make the customer lose the evidence because only successful meals are listed.

scenarios.title: Cancellation races with production start
scenarios.trigger: The cook starts preparation while the customer confirms a cancellation preview.
scenarios.expected: Use authoritative server state and a transactional boundary. Refresh changed terms before commitment; avoid contradictory stock, production, and refund outcomes.

scenarios.title: Confirmed address change request
scenarios.trigger: The customer asks to send a paid order elsewhere.
scenarios.expected: Review serviceability, time, custody, fees, and consent. Do not use an address-book edit to redirect an active courier or assume the new destination is feasible.

scenarios.title: Supplier asks customer to cancel
scenarios.trigger: A cook cannot fulfill and requests a voluntary customer cancellation.
scenarios.expected: Record supplier failure and offer the applicable remedy. Do not impose change-of-mind retention or hide the actual cancellation cause.

scenarios.title: Material edit needs more money
scenarios.trigger: A paid order change increases portions or adds a priced modifier.
scenarios.expected: In M1 use reviewed cancel/reorder or explicit support resolution. A later amendment requires a valid new commitment/payment adjustment and preserves the old outcome on failure.

scenarios.title: Cancellation with no recoverable loss
scenarios.trigger: After cutoff, food is not committed or the cost is recovered elsewhere.
scenarios.expected: Base any retention on lawful disclosed evidenced loss. Do not apply maximum penalties automatically or recover the same loss more than once.

scenarios.title: Serious report without a photo
scenarios.trigger: A customer reports illness, contamination, or an undeclared allergen without images.
scenarios.expected: Triage immediately, advise stopping consumption, notify safety ownership, and contain affected supply as appropriate. Evidence collection cannot delay required customer protection or reporting.

scenarios.title: Repeat refund claimant reports safety issue
scenarios.trigger: An account under abuse review makes a credible serious complaint.
scenarios.expected: Handle urgent food safety independently from fraud investigation. Human review may assess abuse, but cannot automatically suppress the safety case.

scenarios.title: Two agents refund concurrently
scenarios.trigger: Separate agents approve overlapping full/partial refunds.
scenarios.expected: Lock/check remaining refundable balance and use provider idempotency. Prevent over-refund and preserve each decision/audit record.

scenarios.title: Refund submitted but fails
scenarios.trigger: A provider accepts a request then returns failure or no terminal result.
scenarios.expected: Keep processing/failed status, assign an owner, reconcile, and update the customer. Do not close the case as refunded before authoritative completion.

scenarios.title: External help channel unavailable
scenarios.trigger: A WhatsApp link, chat connection, or support notification fails.
scenarios.expected: Keep the in-app case record and an approved fallback with hours/expectations. No response is not agreement and an undelivered message is not presented as read.

scenarios.title: Reorder recipe changed
scenarios.trigger: An old order contains a dish with new ingredients/options or price.
scenarios.expected: Build a fresh review, highlight material differences, and validate current disclosures, stock, date, and total. An old receipt cannot authorize a new allergen profile.

scenarios.title: Reorder conflicts with active kitchen
scenarios.trigger: The old order belongs to a different seller than the current basket.
scenarios.expected: Apply the explicit kitchen conflict flow. Do not combine sellers or duplicate existing quantities without a visible choice.

scenarios.title: Delivery problem damages cook rating
scenarios.trigger: A customer wants to rate a late courier after an otherwise correct meal.
scenarios.expected: Collect appropriate separate feedback and route the actual cause to operations. Avoid attributing delivery failure automatically to meal quality.

scenarios.title: Review exposes private information
scenarios.trigger: A public review contains a phone, exact household location, harassment, or unrelated family detail.
scenarios.expected: Moderate the private/abusive content through a documented process, preserve fair criticism, and allow review/appeal. Safety reports also create private cases.

scenarios.title: Favorite kitchen unavailable today
scenarios.trigger: A saved cook is closed, paused, or not serviceable at the new address.
scenarios.expected: Keep a truthful saved identity with the correct unavailable/next-slot action. A favorite never bypasses eligibility or becomes an automatic order.

scenarios.title: Phone change takeover attempt
scenarios.trigger: An attacker requests a new number or recovery using a message alone.
scenarios.expected: Apply secure verification/recovery, protect active obligations, revoke compromised access, and avoid disclosing another account through lookup responses.

scenarios.title: Deletion with an outstanding refund
scenarios.trigger: A customer requests deletion while money or a complaint is unresolved.
scenarios.expected: Explain necessary retention and provide a secure follow-up route while honoring applicable deletion/marketing rules. Do not erase ledger evidence or block the request indefinitely without basis.

scenarios.title: Revoked device retains access
scenarios.trigger: A cook/courier/admin loses authorization or a customer logs out a device.
scenarios.expected: Enforce server session/object access revocation. Cached private data and deep links cannot continue exposing sensitive records.

scenarios.title: Object ID changed in a request
scenarios.trigger: A user tries another customer order, cook payout, or courier assignment ID.
scenarios.expected: Deny unauthorized object access without revealing private details. Visible role selection is not sufficient authorization.

scenarios.title: Payment token removal during active order
scenarios.trigger: A customer removes a saved provider token after paying.
scenarios.expected: Remove future-use authorization appropriately without erasing the existing transaction/refund reference or breaking necessary reconciliation.

scenarios.title: Push permission denied
scenarios.trigger: The customer or cook refuses system notifications.
scenarios.expected: Keep current orders, required actions, cases, and payment status accessible in-app. Use only approved necessary fallback channels; no false claim that a push was delivered.

scenarios.title: Duplicate or stale notification
scenarios.trigger: Retries send an old ready/cancel/payment event repeatedly.
scenarios.expected: Deduplicate and resolve the linked current state. Never regress status or cause a duplicate financial/courier action from a notification tap.

scenarios.title: Chat promise changes a contract
scenarios.trigger: A cook offers another ingredient, date, fee, or payment destination in chat.
scenarios.expected: Require an authorized reviewed quote/change workflow and informed customer acceptance. Chat alone cannot amend a paid order or give unsupported safety assurances.

scenarios.title: Message fails or remains unanswered
scenarios.trigger: A pre-order question is unsent, unread, or beyond response hours.
scenarios.expected: Display truthful channel state and response expectations; offer support or leave the request unaccepted. Do not treat silence as seller acceptance.

scenarios.title: Harassment or sensitive preview
scenarios.trigger: A message exposes household/health data or abusive contact.
scenarios.expected: Provide reporting/contact restrictions and minimize lock-screen content. Preserve necessary evidence under restricted access without cutting off legitimate order support.

scenarios.title: One future date has no capacity
scenarios.trigger: A seven-delivery purchase has six available dates and one unavailable date.
scenarios.expected: Validate all occurrences before charging using a safe all-or-nothing workflow. Offer explicit revised dates instead of creating an unbacked paid entitlement.

scenarios.title: Discount and fees across seven dates
scenarios.trigger: A hypothetical plan uses seven EGP 350 meals, 5% Bety discount, EGP 35 delivery and EGP 10 service per date.
scenarios.expected: Show food 2,450 minus 122.50 plus 245 delivery plus 70 service = 2,642.50 before tax adjustment, with sponsor and per-occurrence allocation recorded.

scenarios.title: One occurrence canceled eligibly
scenarios.trigger: One of the example plan deliveries is fully cancelable before commitment.
scenarios.expected: Refund its allocated EGP 332.50 food plus 35 delivery plus 10 service = 377.50 before tax adjustment. Update entitlement/liability without retroactive surprise repricing of completed meals.

scenarios.title: Cook unavailable for remaining plan
scenarios.trigger: Illness, leave, eligibility lapse, or missing menu prevents future committed dates.
scenarios.expected: List affected occurrences, offer informed eligible alternatives or refunds, and preserve unresolved liability. Do not automatically substitute another cook or unsafe recipe.

scenarios.title: Plan ends or reschedule fails
scenarios.trigger: The final entitlement is used, or a requested replacement date is unavailable.
scenarios.expected: End a finite plan without auto-charge. Keep the original occurrence valid until an approved reschedule commits, then link replacement and financial allocation.

scenarios.title: Pickup requested at a private home
scenarios.trigger: A household kitchen has no approved public collection arrangement.
scenarios.expected: Hide/block pickup and offer platform delivery or an eligible commercial location. Do not expose the home address to satisfy a cart toggle.

scenarios.title: Mode switch changes fees or offer
scenarios.trigger: A delivery basket switches to eligible pickup before commitment.
scenarios.expected: Revalidate pickup window, address/instructions, charges, and promotion. Present the exact revised quote before acceptance.

scenarios.title: Pickup code reused or wrong person
scenarios.trigger: A code is submitted twice or an unauthorized person claims the food.
scenarios.expected: Verify the authorized collection, consume the handoff once, and record custody. Do not release another order or falsely complete multiple pickups.

scenarios.title: Customer arrives after safe holding limit
scenarios.trigger: A paid pickup customer is late or never arrives.
scenarios.expected: Follow approved holding/no-show policy, contact support, and document food disposition and remedy. Payment does not extend safe holding indefinitely.

scenarios.title: Kitchen not ready at collection
scenarios.trigger: A customer arrives in the agreed window but food is not ready.
scenarios.expected: Show truthful status, provide an operational recovery/remedy, and protect safety. Do not require collection confirmation before actual handoff.

scenarios.title: Request mistaken for paid confirmation
scenarios.trigger: A customer submits dishes, people, budget, and date without an accepted quote.
scenarios.expected: Label it as a request with response expectations. No order commitment/payment occurs until seller, menu, portions, ingredients, timing, and complete price are accepted.

scenarios.title: Expired custom quote accepted
scenarios.trigger: The customer returns after quote expiry or capacity loss.
scenarios.expected: Revalidate and issue a current offer. No old screenshot or chat price automatically reserves production or authorizes payment.

scenarios.title: Catering exceeds safe throughput
scenarios.trigger: A normal meal quantity is multiplied for a large event.
scenarios.expected: Require a reviewed event process, capacity, transport/holding, service scope, and payment/cancellation terms. Do not treat large quantity alone as ordinary checkout eligibility.

scenarios.title: Raw or finish-at-home item confused with ready meal
scenarios.trigger: A customer browses preparation types with different cooking/storage obligations.
scenarios.expected: Label the actual state clearly, enforce separately approved processes, and block incompatible mixed-mode checkout. Do not imply ready-to-eat safety.

scenarios.title: Unsupported dietary or ingredient promise
scenarios.trigger: A custom request asks for therapeutic suitability or guaranteed allergen-free food.
scenarios.expected: Use qualified approved factual review or decline. Neither sales pressure nor a seller chat promise bypasses category restrictions or cross-contact limitations.

scenarios.title: Identity passes but kitchen fails
scenarios.trigger: A seller has a verified identity but no valid production route or critical kitchen remediation remains.
scenarios.expected: Keep sales disabled and communicate precise next steps. Identity approval cannot publish supply or be displayed as food certification.

scenarios.title: Approval expires before meal date
scenarios.trigger: A required permission is valid today but not on a future production date.
scenarios.expected: Block affected future commitments, notify the seller, and list existing affected orders for resolution. Do not rely solely on application-time validity.

scenarios.title: Production moves to another location
scenarios.trigger: A cook changes kitchen or uses an unreviewed family location.
scenarios.expected: Require location-specific eligibility and safety review before new production. Preserve historic location records and review committed orders.

scenarios.title: Assisted application contains an error
scenarios.trigger: A staff member enters documents/capacity on behalf of a cook.
scenarios.expected: Let the cook confirm relevant facts and terms, track the actor, and correct evidence securely. Assistance cannot fabricate consent or hide rejection reasons.

scenarios.title: Payout verification incomplete
scenarios.trigger: The cook passes food review but bank/provider onboarding remains unresolved.
scenarios.expected: Explain the remaining commercial activation requirement and stop unsupported sales/payout promises. Do not collect future seller liabilities through an unapproved flow.

scenarios.title: Several dishes share one oven limit
scenarios.trigger: Each dish individually has stock but their combined batch exceeds practical resources.
scenarios.expected: Enforce a conservative shared kitchen/resource cap. Independent dish counts cannot multiply the approved production capacity.

scenarios.title: Cook reduces capacity below orders
scenarios.trigger: A seller lowers a future limit below already confirmed quantities.
scenarios.expected: Stop further sale, show existing commitments, and raise an operations decision. Never silently cancel or erase paid obligations.

scenarios.title: New price or recipe affects old order
scenarios.trigger: A published meal changes after customers already paid.
scenarios.expected: Version future sales and retain accepted snapshots. Safety-related changes trigger affected-order review instead of blindly honoring an unsafe old recipe.

scenarios.title: Promotion makes cook contribution negative
scenarios.trigger: An offer funds itself from seller proceeds or labor is omitted from costing.
scenarios.expected: Show sponsor, commission basis, full allocated cost/labor, and expected contribution. Require seller agreement; do not silently discount earnings.

scenarios.title: Pause has existing commitments
scenarios.trigger: The cook pauses sales for illness, leave, or workload.
scenarios.expected: Stop new commitments and prominently list affected existing orders with support actions. A pause is not invisible cancellation or a requirement to cook while ill.

scenarios.title: Critical batch check fails
scenarios.trigger: A required measurement, ingredient trace, or other critical control is outside its approved limit.
scenarios.expected: Block readiness/dispatch, isolate affected stock, and route to the qualified safety owner. A courier arrival or paid order cannot override the control.

scenarios.title: Power, water, or equipment failure
scenarios.trigger: Production/holding conditions become uncertain.
scenarios.expected: Pause affected production/sales, record actual times/readings, assess disposition professionally, and resolve orders. Do not rely on smell, taste, or unvalidated reheating.

scenarios.title: Cook reports illness
scenarios.trigger: The responsible food handler cannot safely work.
scenarios.expected: Stop affected production, engage operations/backup under an approved route, and remedy customer commitments. Do not pressure the cook to continue or conceal the event.

scenarios.title: Packing labels mismatch orders
scenarios.trigger: Correct portions are assigned to wrong package IDs or modifiers.
scenarios.expected: Detect at packing/handoff using order/batch/package verification, correct safely, and prevent wrong ingredient/allergen delivery. Preserve an audit trail for any correction.

scenarios.title: Ready action captured offline
scenarios.trigger: The app has not synchronized a cook readiness/check event.
scenarios.expected: Show pending sync and provide the approved support fallback. Do not dispatch from a client-only checkbox or invent a server acceptance timestamp.

scenarios.title: Wrong or replaced courier collects
scenarios.trigger: An obsolete assignment token or unassigned courier attempts pickup.
scenarios.expected: Validate current assignment and revoke old access/codes. The cook verifies custody transfer before releasing private pickup information/packages.

scenarios.title: Seal damaged or route limits exceeded
scenarios.trigger: A courier finds leakage/tampering or cannot meet validated transport conditions.
scenarios.expected: Escalate and prevent unsafe handoff as appropriate, record disposition, and arrange customer remedy. Do not open/repack casually or resell uncertain-custody food.

scenarios.title: Completion code requested too early
scenarios.trigger: A courier asks for the customer delivery PIN at pickup or before arrival.
scenarios.expected: Reject premature completion, explain the code is for actual handoff, and retain a support fallback with audited proof.

scenarios.title: Customer unreachable at destination
scenarios.trigger: Contact attempts fail during the approved waiting period.
scenarios.expected: Keep required conditions, shorten waiting for safety limits, and let support determine a safe resolution. Do not leave with a neighbor/lobby without an approved agreement.

scenarios.title: COD cash differs from collectible
scenarios.trigger: The courier requests extra money or remits less than the authorized amount.
scenarios.expected: Customer sees exact collectible; record collection/remittance separately and raise a discrepancy. Only explicit contractual deductions explain differences, not an assumed delivery fee.

scenarios.title: Customer collections mistaken for revenue
scenarios.trigger: Balances include seller payables, refunds, or future plan obligations.
scenarios.expected: Keep liabilities and platform revenue separate. Cash timing cannot authorize using cook/customer obligations as operating profit.

scenarios.title: Same payable enters two payout runs
scenarios.trigger: Retries or concurrent preparation selects an already scheduled seller balance.
scenarios.expected: Use unique ledger references and atomic eligibility/release checks. Prevent duplicate payout and reconcile authoritative bank/provider outcomes.

scenarios.title: Bank-detail change before payout
scenarios.trigger: A new payout destination is submitted through account change or messaging.
scenarios.expected: Reverify through a trusted path, notify the established contact, and apply approved review/cooling controls. A message alone cannot redirect funds.

scenarios.title: Refund and chargeback overlap
scenarios.trigger: A disputed order also has a provider refund or seller adjustment.
scenarios.expected: Reconcile all linked entries and prevent duplicate recovery. Explain responsibility separately from immediate customer resolution and preserve correcting reversals.

scenarios.title: One disputed order holds all earnings
scenarios.trigger: A small complaint is used to freeze an entire seller balance.
scenarios.expected: Use justified amount-specific holds with reason, review date, owner, and appeal. Unrelated eligible earnings follow the published payout cycle.

scenarios.title: Affected batch includes refunded customers
scenarios.trigger: A recall lookup filters only currently paid or completed orders.
scenarios.expected: Retrieve every affected recipient/order regardless of cancellation/refund state where exposure occurred. Refund history cannot erase safety contact responsibility.

scenarios.title: Support attempts privileged action
scenarios.trigger: An agent tries changing eligibility, payout bank details, or unauthorized refund amount.
scenarios.expected: Enforce action and object permissions server-side, log attempts, and route to the correct role. UI hiding alone is inadequate.

scenarios.title: Configuration changes after acceptance
scenarios.trigger: A fee, cutoff, zone, or cancellation policy is edited.
scenarios.expected: Version future commitments and preserve accepted commercial snapshots. Apply necessary safety containment separately rather than silently repricing old orders.

scenarios.title: Serious hold reopened without evidence
scenarios.trigger: A kitchen is proposed for reactivation after contamination/critical failure.
scenarios.expected: Require documented corrective action, qualified safety review, and the approved second authorization. A commercial deadline cannot dismiss containment.

scenarios.title: Bulk admin action selects wrong scope
scenarios.trigger: A kitchen/batch/zone action would affect more records than intended.
scenarios.expected: Preview scope and commitments, require appropriate confirmation/permission, audit the action, and provide safe containment/correction without losing history.

scenarios.title: Large text or screen reader
scenarios.trigger: RTL, mixed-script address, a modal, and sticky controls are used with assistive settings.
scenarios.expected: Maintain reading/focus order and readable units/prices/errors; keep required options and primary actions reachable. State cannot depend only on color or an icon.

scenarios.title: Offline cache looks purchasable
scenarios.trigger: Catalog content remains visible during an outage.
scenarios.expected: Label stale content and preserve drafts, but require online authoritative quote/capacity/payment commitment. Never accept blind money from cached availability.

scenarios.title: Clock, timezone, or daylight-saving boundary
scenarios.trigger: Device clock is wrong or a Cairo business date crosses a timezone transition.
scenarios.expected: Compute eligibility and cutoff server-side from timezone-aware rules, store UTC instants, and display an unambiguous local accepted date/window.

scenarios.title: Restore replays jobs and provider events
scenarios.trigger: Database/service recovery brings old jobs and payment callbacks back.
scenarios.expected: Reconcile authoritative provider/bank state and deduplicate transitions. Restoration must not duplicate an order, refund, seller payout, or customer notification action.

scenarios.title: Sensitive information enters telemetry
scenarios.trigger: An error/export/log contains IDs, exact household location, OTP, payment secrets, or health notes.
scenarios.expected: Redact/minimize data, restrict access/export, and investigate exposure. Analytics requires only necessary business identifiers and states under the approved privacy policy.
